title.narrative: CSF_Support till nationella och lokala policyer för klimatförändringar
CSF_Support to National and local Climate Change Policies

description.narrative:
Syftet med insatsen är att stödja insatser för att minska avskogningen och växthusgasutsläppen – till år 2030 och 2050. För att uppnå detta huvudmål har tre specifika mål fastställts:
- Mål 1: Att stödja utformningen av en strategi för minskning och begränsning av avskogning på nationell nivå, baserad på utarbetandet av en aktionsplan för att uppnå målen för skogsbruks- och jordbrukssektorerna som fastställts i NDCs för den plurinationella staten Bolivia 2021-2030.
- Mål 2: Att analysera, bedöma och utforma minst en finansiell mekanism för att förbättra genereringen av egna inkomster för den nationella myndigheten för skyddade områden - SERNAP
-Mål 3: Att analysera de ekonomiska konsekvenserna av genomförandet av de åtgärder som identifierats i den regionala strategi för klimatförändringar som utarbetats av departementsregeringen i Santa Cruz, i den så kallade Departmentally Determined Contributions (DDC), och identifiera i) deras kostnadseffektivitet, ii) kostnaden för deras genomförande, iii) deras inverkan på makroekonomiska resultat på departamentsnivå, iv) Jämförelse av den makroekonomiska prognosen – baserad på ett grundscenario (utan DDC).
Tidsramen för insatsen är två och ett halvt år med en aktivitetsperiod på två år (24 månader). Insatsen har en beräknad kostnad på cirka 7 998 480 kronor.

The aim of the intervention is to support efforts to reduce deforestation and GHG-emissions - towards the years 2030 and 2050.
To achieve this main objective, three specific objectives have been established:
- Objective 1: To support the design of a Deforestation Reduction and Mitigation Strategy at the national level, based on the development of a Roadmap to achieve the goals of the Forestry and Agricultural sectors established in the NDC of the Plurinational State of Bolivia 2021-2030
- Objective 2: To analyse, assess and design at least one financial mechanism to improve the generation of own income for the National Authority of Protected Areas - SERNAP
-Objective 3: To analyse the economic impact associated with the implementation of the measures identified in the Departmental Climate Change Strategy developed by the Departmental Government of Santa Cruz, hereinafter called Departmentally Determined Contributions (DDC), identifying i) their cost-efficiency, ii) the cost associated with their implementation, iii) their impact on macroeconomic performance at the departmental level, and iv) the comparison of the macroeconomic projection - based on a baseline scenario (without EDCC).
The timeframe of the intervention is two and half years with an activity period of two years (24 months). The contribution has an estimated cost of about SEK 7 998 480 .

This proposal seeks to contribute to the national and departmental public policies to combat climate change, based on a joint collaboration with academia, civil society and the public sector. The aim is to support efforts to reduce deforestation and CO2eq emissions up to the years 2030 and 2050. To achieve this main objective, three specific objectives have been established: - Objective 1: To support the design of a Deforestation Reduction and Mitigation Strategy at the national level, based on the generation of a Roadmap to achieve the goals of the Forestry and Agricultural sectors established in the NDC of the Plurinational State of Bolivia 2021-2030 - Objective 2: To analyse, assess and design at least one financial mechanism to improve the generation of own income for the National Authority of Protected Areas SERNAP -Objective 3: To analyse the economic impact associated with the implementation of the measures identified in the Climate Change Departmental Strategy developed by the Departmental Government of Santa Cruz, hereinafter called Departmentally Determined Contributions (CDD), identifying i) their cost-efficiency, ii) the cost associated with their implementation, iii) their impact on macroeconomic performance at the departmental, and iv) the comparison of the macroeconomic projection with respect to a baseline scenario (without EDCC).
At the end of the intervention is expected: -The establishment of a Roadmap to reduce and mitigate deforestation in Bolivia, in such a way that it is viable and applicable within the terms established in the updated NDC (and its goals until the year 2030), outlining actions and goals that contribute to achieving the sectoral measures defined for the Forestry and Agricultural sectors. - The design of at least one new financing mechanism for SERNPAC, based on reliable technical information, and the roadmap for its implementation and inclusion in SERNAPs Collection System. - A report that will contain the results of the model simulations that show the macroeconomic effects and the financial needs of the implementation of key climate change mitigation policies in the department of Santa Cruz (aimed at reducing CO2eq emissions in accordance with the CDDs, Bolivian´s NDC and the objectives of CO2eq emissions by 2050). In a complementary and descriptive way, it is planned to identify and analyse the gender implications that the proposed policies may have.

description.narrative: The CSF portfolio has demonstrated excellent performance and strategic relevance during the reporting period, successfully concluding its first phase and initiating a second phase focused on financial sustainability and climate policy. Despite a complex operational context marked by political uncertainty and institutional transitions, the partner has delivered high-impact, evidence-based products that are directly informing national and sub-national policies. Key results across the portfolio are documented below: 1.1. Strategic Policy Influence and High-Level Technical Inputs: * National Deforestation Reduction Strategy: Developed and delivered a high-level technical strategy, forming the basis for sectoral policies to curb forest loss in Bolivia. This document was adopted by the Plurinational Authority of Mother Earth (APMT) and served as the foundational input for further work by other partners, demonstrating its technical utility. Despite the fact that the document was not published as an official document (mainly due to disputes among the public organizations that are part of the forest council/forum), it is known to have been distributed by these organizations to serve as a reference for the construction of other specific strategies, associated with the forest and land-use change sector, which these institutions agreed to develop. * Support for Updated Climate Commitments (NDC 3.0): A critical technical work for Bolivia's updated Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) was made, including cost analysis of mitigation measures, emission balances, and abatement curves for the forestry and agricultural sectors. CSF directly supported the development of the agricultural and forestry chapters of NDC Version 3.0, which were officially submitted to the UNFCCC in November 2025. These chapters are the most important for Bolivia, as both sectors represent more than 80% of the country's total GHG emissions. This positions CSF as a key technical ally to the Ministry of Environment and Water (MMAyA) and the Ministry of Rural Development and Lands (MDRyT) ahead of COP 30. * Sub-National Climate Planning (Santa Cruz): Completed an Economic Impact Study of the Departmental Climate Change Strategy (EDCC) for Santa Cruz. This pioneering macroeconomic model provides a technical framework for sub-national climate management and has generated interest from other departments like Pando, Beni, and Tarija for replication. This study helped position the Government of Santa Cruz as a pioneering subnational government on climate issues and generated key information on the implementation costs of the Departmental Climate Change Strategy. This information was considered in the subnational government's plans to manage funds associated with emission reduction actions and projects in the department. The study was also presented at the GCF Task Force conference, held in the Department of Santa Cruz in 2024. 1.2. Innovative Financial Mechanisms for Conservation: * "Conservation Passport" (Pasaporte Ambiental): Successfully designed, legally approved, and launched an innovative voluntary donation mechanism for the National Protected Areas Service (SERNAP). The launch in December 2024 garnered significant public and institutional support, and the mechanism has been recognized as a key tool within the Permanent Financing Project (PFP). Its design was backed by a scientific publication in the journal Land. The mechanism was paralyzed twice after its launch, due to changes in authorities at SERNAP and internal problems in that institution, but it was successfully re-launched at EXPOCRUZ (Santa Cruz International Fair), in September 2025. * Tourist Fee Optimization (SISCO): Provided technical studies to optimize the tourist fee structure in the Cotapata Protected Area. The results, also published in the journal Sustainability, are being managed by SERNAP for implementation and serve as a replicable model. Work has begun to apply this model in the Amboró and Otuquis protected areas. * Benefit Distribution Mechanism (MDB): Delivered a comprehensive design for a results-based distribution mechanism under the LEAF Coalition, establishing a solid technical basis for future implementation in Pando and Charagua Iyambae. The technical report of this distribution mechanism is accompanied by an Excel sheet that can be adapted/adjusted to other similar carbon projects in the country. 1.3. Effective Communication and Platform Coordination: * EU-Sweden Platform Communication: Strategy: Successfully executed a short-term project (Feb-May 2025) to enhance the visibility of the EU-Sweden Environmental Platform. This resulted in four high-quality inspirational videos, infographics, and a communicators' workshop that strengthened collaboration and built a common narrative among 14 partner organizations. * Strategic Dissemination: Across all components, CSF demonstrated a strong capacity for strategic communication, including scientific publications, policy briefs, informative booklets, and active participation in national and international events, ensuring high visibility for both its work and the support from Sida/UE.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
